subject: Science
textbooks: Assessment of Practical Skills in Science, Class IX (CBSE)

chapters.name: Cell
topics: Discovery of cell
Plant and animal cells
Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
Cell as the structural and functional unit of life; key organelles (nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplast, endoplasmic reticulum, vacuoles, plasma membrane, cell wall)
Permeability of cell membranes
Cellular division and cancer
Recent advancement in cell biology
outcomes: Differentiates plant and animal cells, prokaryotes and eukaryotes
Differentiates diffusion and osmosis and demonstrates osmosis
Explains the role of mitosis and meiosis in similarities and variations
Prepares slides to observe cell structure

chapters.name: Tissues
topics: Tissues: introduction and importance; levels of organisation
Plant tissues: meristematic (types, function) and permanent (types, structure, function)
Animal tissues: epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous
Elementary idea of the musculoskeletal system
Care of the musculoskeletal system: injuries, postural care, nutrition and exercise
outcomes: Differentiates plant and animal tissues, meristematic and permanent, simple and complex tissues
Relates tissue structure to function
Correlates muscles, cartilage and bones in movement

chapters.name: Reproduction
topics: Forms of reproduction: sexual and asexual; types of asexual reproduction
Sexual reproduction in flowering plants: flower and its parts, pollination, fertilisation, seed dispersal
Sexual reproduction in humans: reproductive systems, gametes, fertilisation, pregnancy and embryo development, menstrual cycle
Reproductive health and hygiene
Introduction to birth control methods and their importance
outcomes: Compares asexual and sexual reproduction
Explains pollination and fertilisation
Differentiates ovule and seed, ovary and fruit
Explains how sexual reproduction introduces variation

chapters.name: Diversity
topics: Importance of classification
Five kingdoms and their key features with examples
Major divisions of animals and plants
Binomial nomenclature
Acellular entities: viruses
outcomes: Classifies organisms into five kingdoms by cellular organisation and ecological role
Applies binomial nomenclature
Recognises the three domains of classification

chapters.name: Exploring Mixtures and their Separation
topics: Homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures
Solutions, suspensions, colloids and their properties
Concentration of solutions: mass by mass, mass by volume and volume by volume percentage
Separation techniques: crystallisation, distillation, paper chromatography, sublimation, centrifugation, coagulation
outcomes: Classifies mixtures as solutions, suspensions or colloids
Calculates the concentration of solutions
Explains the principles behind separation techniques
Analyses solubility graphs

chapters.name: Structure of an Atom
topics: Atoms as the basic units of elements; subatomic particles
Atomic models: Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr
Distribution of electrons (first 18 elements)
Symbols
Valency as combining capacity
Atomic number, mass number, isotopes and isobars
outcomes: Differentiates electrons, protons and neutrons
Distributes electrons in K, L, M, N shells
Calculates subatomic particles from atomic and mass numbers
Applies IUPAC symbols for the first eighteen elements

chapters.name: Atoms and Molecules
topics: Law of conservation of mass
Law of constant proportions
Dalton's atomic theory
Molecules of elements and covalent compounds and their properties
Ions, ionic compounds and their properties
Writing chemical formulae
Molecular mass and formula unit mass
outcomes: Explains the laws of chemical combination and Dalton's theory
Calculates ionic charge, valency, molecular and formula unit mass
Writes chemical formulae of simple compounds

chapters.name: Motion
topics: Displacement, velocity, acceleration
Graphical representation of straight-line motion (constant velocity and constant acceleration)
Kinematic equations for constant acceleration by graphical method
Elementary idea of uniform circular motion
outcomes: Plots and interprets position-time and velocity-time graphs
Derives kinematic equations graphically
Calculates unknown quantities using kinematic equations
Derives the speed of uniform circular motion

chapters.name: Force and Laws of Motion
topics: Force; balanced and unbalanced forces
Force of friction
Newton's first, second and third laws of motion
outcomes: States and explains Newton's three laws
Calculates force using F = ma
Applies the laws to everyday events

chapters.name: Work, Energy and Simple Machines
topics: Work done by a constant force
Work-energy theorem
Kinetic and potential energy and their interconversion
Conservation of energy
Power
Simple machines and mechanical advantage (pulley, inclined plane, lever)
outcomes: Calculates work, kinetic energy, potential energy and power
States the law of conservation of energy
Calculates the mechanical advantage of simple machines

chapters.name: Sound
topics: Production of sound
Propagation as a longitudinal wave through a medium
Graphical representation of sound waves
Characteristics: wavelength, frequency, time period, amplitude, intensity, speed
Human perception of sound: pitch, loudness
Propagation in different media
Reflection of sound: echo, reverberation, echolocation
outcomes: Relates time period and frequency
Derives and calculates the speed of sound
Applies reflection of sound to echo and reverberation

chapters.name: Earth as a System: Energy, Matter & Life
topics: Earth as an interconnected system
Solar radiation, the electromagnetic spectrum and the speed of light
Solar energy interaction with the Earth's surface and differential heating
Differential warming causes winds
Biogeochemical cycles: water, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen
Human impact on the Earth's system
outcomes: Explains interconnections between the Earth's spheres
Relates differential heating to breezes and weather
Explains biogeochemical cycles and their role in environmental balance

notes: The course structure maps textbook chapters 2-13 to units; chapter 1 is not listed under any assessed unit.
